findings.title: `queued` default is set once at import time, not per instance.
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` runs once, when the class is defined. Every `AssignmentSource` built afterwards (including through `from_integration`) gets the worker's import timestamp, not the time the assignment was queued. Anything that reads `queued`, such as ordering or staleness checks for the sync-cycle logic, gets a wrong and possibly hours-old value. Use `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

held.title: Task kwargs now carry a raw `datetime` that may not serialize.
held.body: `assignment_source.to_dict()` uses `asdict`, so the `queued` field stays a `datetime` object inside the Celery kwargs. If the task broker uses JSON serialization (Sentry has been moving tasks to JSON), `apply_async` will fail on every inbound-webhook assignment. With pickle it works, but on the worker `from_dict` gets back whatever the serializer produced. I could not see the serializer config from here. To be safe, serialize `queued` as an ISO string (or a timestamp) in `to_dict` and parse it back in `from_dict`.
